queries: The adaptive traffic signal system operates through a distributed reinforcement learning mechanism where intersections learn optimal timing policies through interaction with their environment and neighbors. Each intersection implements a reinforcement learning algorithm that receives rewards based on local performance metrics (throughput, queue length, delay). The learning algorithm explores different timing strategies and updates its policy based on the rewards received. Additionally, intersections share their learned policies with neighbors, allowing the network to collectively develop optimal strategies through distributed learning. The system gradually improves its performance over time as each intersection learns from its own experiences and those of its neighbors.
sources: The Lotus Effect: Superhydrophobicity and Self-Cleaning
